sources.quote: Constance had a boy this morning at ten forty-five. She is quite happy and doing well but can not see anyone for some days. She sends her love.
sources.context: Telegram, Wilde to Otho Holland Lloyd, 5 June 1885, Chelsea (MS Holland) - quoted whole. The boy is Cyril Wilde (1885-1915), who was educated at Radley, became a professional soldier and was killed in action in the First World War.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: Wilde wiring his brother-in-law within hours of Cyril's birth.

sources.quote: My dear Otho, Thank you so much for your lovely present. It will be of great use to me as it is by far the best book on Japanese Art that I know. It really was most kind of you to think of it. I hope little Otho is better and that Nellie is not working herself too hard nursing.
sources.context: Wilde to Otho Holland Lloyd, [postmark 31 August 1886], 16 Tite Street (MS Holland) - quoted whole. The editors note that two books on Japanese art were among those sold at the Tite Street sale in 1895. 'Little Otho' is his nephew; Nellie is Otho's wife.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: The ordinary family footing - a present, and asking after a sick nephew.

name: Otho Holland Lloyd
bio: Constance Wilde's elder brother, and so Wilde's brother-in-law. Five of Wilde's letters to him survive, from 1885 to 1898 - the first a telegram announcing the birth of Cyril, the last two from the exile. He and his wife Nellie had a son also called Otho.
bio_note: The volume's Index of Recipients. Five letters at printed 261, 262, 285, 1036 and 1055.
